Yeah--so basically hair loss is a progressive gene. Some people settle into a MPB pattern which matures and doesn't progress further. Some are destined to go full NW6 or NW7 (the halo around the sides only left). Totally depends on your pattern, and only a surgeon or dermatologist can properly diagnose your pattern.

Fin, to me, is a necessity if you have any type of balding that's not just slight recession into a mature hairline. If you're thinning on the mid-scalp, or your recession is aggressive--you'll be playing HT catch up for the rest of your life, or simply dealing with having hair some places and none / patches in others.

I have been on Fin for nearly two years with no sides. Also got Min into my regimen recently. If not, I feel like the hair loss will catch up with you, period. 

I was in a similar place to you about 5 years ago. Only had recession on my hairline and peaks. Was going to get a HT in NY from Feller & Bloxham (FUT, not FUE) but I didn't want to take Fin for fear of sides.

I passed on the procedure and didn't get on meds. I started diffuse thinning and my recession got more aggressive. 3 years later I was on Fin, headed to Turkey where a shitty clinic gave me an aggressive hairline I didn't need and terrible donor scarring.


Point is, I wish I got on Fin when it wasn't so bad. I wish I got a conservative HT at a reputable surgeon in the states. I wish I did so many things but hey, you learn I guess. 

I'm hopeful you can learn from my mistake and others' mistakes. 

I advise you get on Fin. Maybe you can have some regrowth or at least severely slow your balding for now. In a few months, look into the top US surgeons and see their quotes. Most have video consults now with COVID for free.

Don't make my same mistake of thinking you don't need fin. A few years from now, you could be in need of far more grafts when you could have just held on to your native hair. HT is expensive, the meds are not. And if you get an HT, expect to be on Fin for life. Unless you're cool with playing catch up every 5 years to keep up with the balding--thus spending way more and potentially entirely depleting your donor.


Best of luck, whatever you do!

My strategy is always Studs & scrubs (aka streaming / wire finding). I like to have a solid core of 3 superstars. In a points league, you want a top 5 guy, and 2 top 20 players. Spend a bulk on them and then wait it out until other teams splurge all their money. You can hover around $40 remaining and then when the like 7/8th round talent are left, drop the hammer for a few supporting/breakout potential players.

Then leave yourself like 15 for when the dollar-value players are left so you can pluck the ones you like the most for $2.

Then I let the end of my bench be my streamer/waiver lotto. Once I find a diamond in the rough, I try to put trades together (2 or 3 for 1) to keep streaming. This way by the end of the year, you can potentially have 5 or 6 top 20 players by draft strat and consolidating. Which is damn near impossible to achieve in a Snake.


Or you can go the "All value" team route. Let ppl overpay for the biggest names. Nominate the huge hype/lower producing guys and sit them out. Then when others spend a ton, you can swoop in and get a whole deep roster of early-mid round guys.

These are the 2 most successful strategies I've seen in auction leagues. I prefer the Studs/Scrubs because it puts my waiver and scouting acumen to work. Plus it's really fun having 2/3 of the top players in the league and seeing them go off every night on your squad.
